PullRequest.Title: Use Copilot SDK APIs to discover customizations

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The exact timer value, Delayer semantics, and fully awaited create/restore call paths are explicit in the repository. Magnitude beyond the guaranteed 100 ms depends on discovery duration, but the mechanism and critical-path delay do not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A 100 ms scheduled timer wait on the session creation and restoration critical path, followed by customization filesystem/RPC work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The fixed delay is paid once for every newly created or restored Copilot session, independent of workspace size; the subsequent discovery cost still scales with customization roots and files.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: At least 100 ms of avoidable session creation/restoration latency before the first session snapshot can be published
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The constructor called `_queueRefresh(false, 0)`, so the initial discovery task was scheduled immediately; only watcher-driven follow-up refreshes used `REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS`.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The constructor now omits the delay argument, so `Delayer.trigger` uses its 100 ms default before starting the initial refresh.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line `this._settled = this._queueRefresh(false);` replaces `this._queueRefresh(false, 0)`, directly moving initial discovery behind the 100 ms default debounce.
Findings.Title: Run the initial customization refresh without the debounce
Findings.Impact: Creating a Copilot session blocks in `AgentService.createSession` while `provider.getSessionCustomizations()` reaches `getCustomizationsSettled()` and waits for `whenSettled()`. Restoring a session has the same awaited path. Every create/restore therefore waits at least 100 ms before customization discovery even begins, delaying the first usable snapshot.
Findings.Evidence: `REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS` is 100 and `_queueRefresh` forwards its default delay to `Delayer.trigger`. `CopilotAgent.getSessionCustomizations` awaits `pluginController.getCustomizationsSettled()`, which awaits `entry.whenSettled()`, and `AgentService.createSession` awaits that provider call before registering initial state. The modified test also changed from observing work after 50 ms to waiting `REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS + 200`, corroborating the scheduling change.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep debounce for change bursts, but pass `0` for the constructor's initial `_queueRefresh` as before (or otherwise start the first refresh immediately).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event's all-keys semantics, one-listener-per-session ownership, full refresh call paths, and concurrent all-session publisher are explicit. The exact number of simultaneously live sessions and filesystem duration vary by user, affecting severity but not the fan-out mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem resolves/scans and, in discover mode, Copilot SDK IPC requests and subprocess-side discovery work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each unrelated root-config event triggers one full refresh per live session entry. In the default scan mode this is roughly the configured discovery-root traversal per session (13 roots in the updated tests, plus recursive hook/instruction contents); in discover mode it is three content-discovery RPCs per warm entry, plus local hook scans and watcher-stat resolves. Root-config handling starts these session publishes concurrently, so cost grows as O(active sessions × discovery roots/files) or 3 × active sessions RPCs.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Bursty excessive filesystem I/O or SDK IPC/subprocess work, increasing config-update latency and contending with active agent-host work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Session-discovered entries refreshed on filesystem watcher changes only. A root-config action republished all sessions, but already-settled live entries did not re-run their disk discovery merely because an unrelated root key changed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every `SessionDiscoveredEntry` now subscribes to the payload-less `onDidRootConfigChange` and unconditionally queues a discovery refresh, even when `sessionCustomizationDiscoveryMode` is unchanged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT listener at line 3221 invokes `_queueRefresh(true)` for every root-config event; no per-session config-triggered discovery existed before this hunk.
Findings.Title: Refresh sessions only when the discovery mode changes
Findings.Impact: Changing any host setting—telemetry, permissions, proxy, auto-approve, model-related options, and others—causes all live Copilot session entries to rescan customization trees. With SDK discovery enabled, each warm session issues three concurrent SDK RPCs; multiple sessions create a 3N request burst. The root-config side effect simultaneously republishes every session and awaits these queued refreshes.
Findings.Evidence: `IAgentConfigurationService.onDidRootConfigChange` explicitly fires for every `RootConfigChanged` action and carries no changed key; the GitHub endpoint service documents this and guards by comparing its derived value. The added listener has no such guard. Its `_queueRefresh` reaches `_discovery.scan` (filesystem traversal) in the default mode or `_discovery.discover` in SDK mode; the latter calls `agents.discover`, `instructions.discover`, and `skills.discover` in `Promise.all`. `AgentSideEffects._publishAllSessionCustomizations` iterates every session on each root-config action without a limiter.
Findings.Recommendation: Store the last effective discovery mode in the entry, re-read it on root-config events, and queue a refresh only when that value actually changes, matching the existing derived-value guard pattern.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or restore a Copilot session while using the default local-scan discovery mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `AgentService.createSession` awaits `provider.getSessionCustomizations`; restore awaits the same call in its `Promise.all`. That reaches `SessionPluginController.getCustomizationsSettled`, which awaits the entry's initial refresh before the first customization-bearing session state can progress. The diff places a 100 ms timer before discovery begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the `Delayer`'s 100 ms default before running initial discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per newly instantiated session-discovery entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial refresh explicitly passed delay 0; only change-driven refreshes used the 100 ms debounce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks the awaited customization result and therefore session creation/restoration state publication

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and scan workspace/user customization roots, recursively scanning relevant nested content and creating watchers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately 13 configured roots per session, with additional resolves proportional to nested hook/instruction/skill directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scan occurred immediately on the initial path, without the newly added 100 ms wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish after the timer before the initial customization snapshot is returned

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed delay per created/restored session, followed by traversal of the configured workspace/user customization roots (13 roots in the updated tests) and recursive hook/instruction/skill contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The 13-ish root scans are launched through `Promise.all` inside one entry. Different session creates/restores can scan concurrently; there is no cross-session limiter or shared scan. A single entry's subsequent events are debounced/canceled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A `SessionDiscoveredEntry` retains the settled customizations and watchers, but a newly created/restored entry is cold and has no cross-session cache. Warm reads await the already-settled promise unless a refresh was queued.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: timer default, changed constructor argument, and awaited call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem duration and session-create frequency vary, but the extra 100 ms is deterministic for every cold entry.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression: the initial debounce adds a guaranteed avoidable 100 ms to an important session startup/restore path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or refresh a session with SDK discovery mode enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold entry, `getSessionCustomizations` waits for Copilot client availability, three discovery-path RPCs, then three content-discovery RPCs plus local hook scanning/watcher resolution. Warm watcher refreshes skip discovery-path RPCs but still await three content RPCs and local filesystem work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three concurrent RPCs on the first successful discovery per session entry; zero on warm refreshes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK discovery mode and these RPCs did not exist; local scan was used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three must settle before content discovery starts

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three concurrent RPCs per discovery refresh per session entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No SDK content-discovery RPCs; local filesystem scan populated session customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three must settle before the customization result is returned

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively discover local hook JSON/settings files and resolve watcher roots/ancestors
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Hook roots and their nested directories, plus one batched `resolveAll` over effective discovered directories and unique ancestors
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hooks were included in the single local scan; the new SDK mode separately performs local hook scanning and watcher-stat reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with content RPCs but must finish before return

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start/await the CopilotClient when SDK discovery is selected
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced client startup globally when no client exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session customization discovery did not require the Copilot SDK client to be running.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold client startup precedes every discovery RPC and blocks the customization result

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One project path per session; content and mapping work scale with discovered agents, instruction sources, skills, hook files, and directory depth. Across sessions, RPC count scales per session rather than per unique working directory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three path RPCs run concurrently; after they finish, three content RPCs, hook scanning, and watcher updates run concurrently. One entry coalesces bursty watcher events using a 100 ms Delayer and cancels its prior refresh, but entries have no cross-session limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `_discoveredDirectories` caches discovery-path results for the entry lifetime, so cold success costs three path RPCs and warm refreshes do not. Content discovery is always fresh. There is no cross-session cache or request coalescing, and negative/failure results from the caught path-discovery block are cached as the returned hook-only list after successful assignment.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: RPC counts, cache placement, ordering, and awaited critical path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC and cold subprocess startup duration depend on environment. The mode is opt-in/defaults to scan, so the base six-RPC cold path is an intentional feature tradeoff rather than an additional finding by itself.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for the intended opt-in SDK source itself; its expensive boundaries are relevant to the reported unfiltered config-event fan-out and initial timer delay.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply any root-level agent-host configuration change while sessions are live
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `RootConfigChanged` synchronously fires the payload-less configuration event. Every live `SessionDiscoveredEntry` now queues a refresh. `AgentSideEffects` also republishes all sessions, and each `getSessionCustomizations` waits for the queued per-entry refresh before publishing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full local customization rescan for each live session entry in default mode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scan per live session per root-config event; each scan covers the configured roots and nested content
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Live settled entries were not invalidated by unrelated root keys; filesystem watcher changes drove their refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The concurrent session republish waits for each affected entry's scan before its state can update

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Three Copilot SDK content-discovery requests per warm session in discover mode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 3 × live discover-mode session entries per root-config event, with three additional path RPCs for any cold entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-entry root-config listener forced these SDK requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each session's republish waits for all three RPCs and local discovery work

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live/restored Copilot session entries multiplied by discovery roots/files in scan mode, or by three warm content RPCs plus hook/watcher filesystem work in discover mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each entry debounces its own events, but there is no coalescing across sessions. `_publishAllSessionCustomizations` starts one asynchronous publish per session without a limiter; discover mode therefore produces up to 3N simultaneous content RPCs for N warm entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing entries retain customizations and SDK discovery paths, but the added listener bypasses the useful settled-state fast path by forcing a fresh content scan/discovery. The listener does not cache or compare the effective discovery mode; unrelated keys invalidate every entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: event all-key semantics, per-entry listener, refresh bodies, and unbounded all-session publisher are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously live sessions and frequency of settings changes vary, but root config covers many unrelated routinely editable settings and the N-session fan-out is deterministic once triggered.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary-fanout regression. The listener should compare the prior/effective discovery mode and invalidate only when that setting changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit customization files while a session is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filesystem watcher changes signal the entry, which waits the intended 100 ms debounce and then refreshes before emitting updated customization state. This is off the immediate typing/render path but controls when customization UI/state reflects file edits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watcher notification followed by local scan or hook/watcher resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective refresh per entry per debounced event burst
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Watcher-driven local rescans already existed and used the same debounce/coalescing mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines customization update latency but is not on an active turn's core request path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Three SDK content-discovery RPCs after a debounced watcher event in discover mode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three per affected entry per effective burst
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File edits caused local rescans only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before changed customizations are published

Scenarios.ScalingInput: File-event burst frequency, number of affected session entries (especially shared user-home roots), and customization tree size; SDK mode adds three RPCs per effective debounced refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one entry, events coalesce into one delayed refresh and an in-flight refresh is canceled when superseded. Across sessions watching shared user-home paths, each entry refreshes independently with no global coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scan mode performs a fresh local scan. Discover mode reuses cached discovery directories but refreshes content RPCs and local hooks/watchers. Equality checks suppress unchanged publication after work completes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-entry behavior; lower only for typical simultaneous session count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Shared-home watcher fan-out depends on how many session entries remain live and which SDK paths are returned.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: per-entry debounce/cancellation is intentional and bounded; cross-session cost is concretely problematic when the new unrelated root-config listener forces it, which is reported separately.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and paginated diffs. Reported the deterministic initial 100 ms critical-path delay and the unfiltered root-config-to-per-session discovery fan-out. Checked SDK RPC/subprocess boundaries, local filesystem traversal/watchers, cache lifetimes, cancellation/coalescing, session ownership/disposal, and test-only reverse-resource helpers. No concrete unbounded retention, cleanup leak, serialization amplification, rendering/layout regression, or independently reportable SDK-mode cost was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
